title: Population Census of Japan (国勢調査)
notes: The spine of the whole exercise. Quinquennial from 1920, so every base year in the 1920–1950 window is covered except the 1945 extraordinary census taken in November after the surrender. City (shi) totals are published for every round. Note the boundary problem: Tokyo City was 35 wards until 1943, when it was merged into Tokyo-to, so 1940 and 1950 figures are not the same unit.

title: e-Stat portal — historical census tables
notes: Downloadable Excel/CSV of the historical census volumes, including the pre-war rounds. Where you want numbers rather than page images this is the place to start.

title: Historical Statistics of Japan (日本長期統計総覧)
notes: Chapter 2 is population. Gives long runs for the largest cities on consistent definitions, which is exactly what a size ranking needs.

title: NDL Digital Collections (国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション)
notes: Where the colonial statistical yearbooks actually live: 日本帝国統計年鑑, 朝鮮総督府統計年報, 台湾総督府統計書, 樺太庁統計書, 南洋庁統計年鑑. Full-text search now works across much of it.

title: Statistical Yearbook of the Japanese Empire (日本帝国統計年鑑)
region_covered: Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Karafuto, Kwantung, Nan'yō
notes: The single volume that puts naichi and all the colonies side by side. Useful precisely because the categories are the empire's own.

title: Annual Statistical Report of the Government-General of Chōsen (朝鮮総督府統計年報)
notes: Annual population by province and by fu (city). Breaks out Japanese, Korean and other residents separately, which matters for reading the colonial port cities.

title: Census of Chōsen (朝鮮国勢調査報告)
notes: Korea was enumerated on the Japanese census cycle from 1925. The 1944 round is a wartime simplified count and should be treated as an estimate.

title: KOSIS historical population statistics
notes: Retrospective series that reproduce the colonial census figures on modern boundaries. Handy for a cross-check, though the reconstruction is not always transparent.

title: Taiwan Statistical Abstract of the Past Fifty-One Years (臺灣省五十一年來統計提要)
notes: Compiled in 1946 from the Japanese colonial records. The best single source for Taiwanese city populations across the whole colonial period, on consistent definitions.

title: Statistical Book of the Government-General of Taiwan (臺灣總督府統計書)
notes: Annual, with population by street and district. Taiwan also ran full censuses in 1905 and 1915 and then on the Japanese cycle from 1920.

title: Taiwan Studies digital resources
notes: Digitised colonial-period statistics and the historical GIS layers that go with them.

title: Manchoukuo Year Book / 滿洲國年鑑
author_or_publisher: Manchuria Daily News / Tōa Keizai Chōsakyoku
notes: English-language editions exist for 1932–1943. City populations are police-registration counts, not a census, and are consistently soft.

title: Manchukuo Provisional Population Census 1940 (臨時國勢調査)
notes: The one real enumeration Manchukuo carried out. Everything else for the region is registration data.

title: South Manchuria Railway reports and statistics
notes: Mantetsu's research department produced the most detailed economic and demographic surveys of the region. Its city figures for the railway zone are better than the state's.

title: Statistical Abstract of the Republic of China (中華民國統計提要)
author_or_publisher: Directorate-General of Budget Accounting and Statistics
notes: Republican China never took a modern census. These are compiled from provincial and municipal returns of very uneven quality; treat as order-of-magnitude.

title: The China Year Book
notes: An English-language annual with municipal population tables, treaty-port figures and foreign-resident counts. Widely used at the time and easy to cite.

title: China Handbook 1937–1945
notes: The Nationalist government's own wartime compilation. Openly propagandistic in places but the administrative and municipal tables are usable.

title: First National Population Census of the PRC (第一次全国人口普查)
notes: The first real Chinese census. Three years past the window, but for many Chinese cities it is the earliest trustworthy number and a good check on the 1930s estimates.

title: China Historical GIS (CHGIS)
notes: Not population, but authoritative on where administrative seats were and when they moved — which is what the provincial-capital variant depends on.

title: Census of India
region_covered: British India, princely states, Burma to 1937, Ceylon separately
notes: Decennial and outstandingly good. Volume I part II tables give town populations down to small towns. The 1941 round was curtailed by the war — tabulation was abandoned for much of it — so 1931 and 1951 are the solid anchors.

title: Census of India report volumes (digitised)
notes: Scanned provincial volumes. The Imperial Tables in each provincial report are where town-level figures actually are.

title: Census of Ceylon
notes: Ceylon was enumerated separately from India. The 1946 round is the useful late-window figure.

title: A Report on the 1931 Census of British Malaya
region_covered: Straits Settlements, Federated and Unfederated Malay States
notes: The standard pre-war Malayan enumeration, with town populations and a full communal breakdown.

title: A Report on the 1947 Census of Population (Malayan Union and Singapore)
notes: The first post-war count. Reading it against 1931 shows the war's demographic damage directly.

title: Report on the Census of the Colony of Hong Kong / Hong Kong Blue Book
notes: The Hong Kong Government Reports Online archive at HKU. There was no census between 1931 and 1961, so 1941 and post-war figures are estimates — and the wartime swing was enormous, from about 1.6 million in 1941 to about 600,000 in 1945 after the Japanese deportations.

title: Volkstelling 1930 (Census of the Netherlands Indies)
author_or_publisher: Departement van Landbouw Nijverheid en Handel
notes: Eight volumes, and the only full enumeration of the Indies. Town populations are in the regional volumes. Nothing comparable exists again until the Indonesian census of 1961.

title: Statistisch Jaaroverzicht van Nederlandsch-Indië
author_or_publisher: Centraal Kantoor voor de Statistiek Batavia
notes: Annual, and fills the gaps either side of the 1930 census.

title: Census of the Philippines
author_or_publisher: Bureau of the Census and Statistics
notes: Three enumerations bracketing the war. The 1939 and 1948 pair is the best before-and-after in the whole region.

title: Population Census of Thailand (สำมะโนประชากร)
notes: Bangkok and Thonburi were separate provinces and are enumerated separately until 1971; add them together for a city figure.

title: Annuaire statistique de l'Indochine
author_or_publisher: Direction des Services Économiques Gouvernement Général de l'Indochine
notes: On Gallica. Indochina took no true census; these are administrative counts, and the Chinese population of Cholon in particular is inconsistently handled from year to year.

title: Census of India 1931 vol. XI (Burma) and Burma Census 1941/1953
notes: Burma was censused with India to 1931 and separately after separation in 1937. The 1941 returns were largely destroyed in the invasion, so 1931 and the 1953 sample census are the anchors.

title: Colonial Office Annual Reports (Blue Books)
region_covered: Hong Kong, Malaya, Borneo, Ceylon, Fiji, Solomons, Gilberts
notes: Population estimates for every British colony and protectorate, year by year. Uneven, but often the only figure for the small Pacific and Borneo territories.

title: Anuário Estatístico do Ultramar / Boletim Oficial de Timor
notes: Thin, but the only official source for Dili, Macao and Goa. Macao's wartime population is a special case — it roughly trebled with refugees from Hong Kong and Canton and no one counted them properly.

title: Soviet censuses of 1926 1939 and 1959
notes: Demoscope Weekly hosts the city tables from all three. The 1939 census was itself a politically corrected replacement for the suppressed 1937 one, so treat totals with care; city figures are less affected than national ones.

title: Sixteenth Census of the United States: Territories and Possessions
notes: Covers Honolulu and Agana. Guam was enumerated in 1940 and then occupied in December 1941.

title: Statistical Yearbook of the South Seas Bureau (南洋庁統計年鑑)
notes: Micronesian settlement populations, with Japanese and Okinawan settlers counted separately from islanders. Essential for Saipan, where by 1937 the settlers heavily outnumbered the Chamorro and Carolinian population.

title: Annual Reports to the League of Nations on the Administration of Mandated Territories
region_covered: South Seas Mandate, New Guinea, Nauru, Western Samoa
notes: The League archive in Geneva. Japan reported annually on the Nan'yō until it left the League in 1935 and then continued for some years; these reports carry district populations.

title: United Nations Demographic Yearbook
notes: The first issues (1948–1952) carry city populations from the immediate post-war censuses, and often reprint the last pre-war figure alongside — a quick way to bracket the window.

title: The Statesman's Year-Book
notes: An annual with city populations for every country and colony, drawn from official returns. Not a primary source, but for obscure places — Kengtung, Port Blair, Brunei Town, Kyzyl — it is often the only accessible one, and you can read the same city across successive years.

title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 14th edition and its yearbooks
notes: Useful mainly as a period cross-check: it tells you what figure was current at the time, which is not always the figure historians now accept.

title: Four Thousand Years of Urban Growth: An Historical Census
notes: The standard historical city-size compilation, with entries at 1900, 1925 and 1950. Chandler's estimates are reconstructions and have been criticised for method, especially in Asia, but they give a consistent cross-regional ranking, which is what a four-tier scheme actually needs.

title: Spatializing 6,000 years of global urbanization (dataset)
author_or_publisher: Meredith Reba, Femke Reitsma, Karen Seto
notes: Chandler and Modelski geocoded and published as CSV in Scientific Data. The easiest way to get a machine-readable historical city-size series, with the same caveats as Chandler.

title: International Historical Statistics: Africa Asia and Oceania 1750–2005
notes: Table A4 in each regional section gives populations of the principal towns, drawn from official censuses and footnoted to them. The fastest way to assemble a consistent cross-country table if you have library access.

title: Populstat historical population statistics
notes: City-level historical series by country, each with its source noted. The site is defunct but fully archived. Unrefereed, so treat it as a finding aid pointing back to the censuses rather than as an authority.

title: City Population
notes: Carries census series back to the 1920s–1940s for Japan, Korea, Taiwan, India, Indonesia and the Philippines, each row tied to its census date. The most convenient modern check on a colonial-era figure.

title: Wikidata population statements (P1082 with point-in-time P585)
notes: Queryable by SPARQL and the source of the machine-harvested columns in cities.csv. Coverage for 1920–1950 in this region is patchy and strongly biased towards Japan and India, where census series have been imported wholesale; for China, Southeast Asia and the Pacific it is close to empty. Every statement should be traced back to its stated reference before being trusted.

title: Japan Statistical Yearbook (日本統計年鑑) city population series
notes: Post-war annual. The 1949–1952 issues carry the 1947 extraordinary census and the 1950 census by city, including the scale of the wartime urban evacuation.

title: HathiTrust Digital Library
notes: Where many of the colonial yearbooks above are findable in full text when the Internet Archive copy is missing. Search-only access for in-copyright volumes still lets you confirm a page and a figure.

title: 昭和五年 臺灣總督府統計書 — 第35表 戶口靜態總表, 第37表 地方別現住人口
notes: Published 1932; the figures are those of the household registers at the end of 1930. Table 35 gives the colony and the eight jurisdictions with the Indigenous Peoples 「蕃人」 in a column apart; table 37 gives the seven 市 and forty-five 郡, which exclude them. pp. 28–37.

title: 昭和五年国勢調査最終報告書 — 市ノ人口 p16
notes: The twenty-eight 市 of 100,000 and over at the census of 1 October 1930.

title: 臺灣總督府第四十五統計書 (昭和16年) — 第16表 市街庄別常住戸口
notes: The resident (常住) population at the end of 1941, from the household and alien registers: 11 市, 51 郡 and 2 支廳, pp. 20–33. Every row balances on its five registers and on male plus female, and the 64 sum exactly to the eight prefecture totals and to 6,249,468.
